title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing and padding minimization v30
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Optimized dynamic batching by sequence length with bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics; KV-cache-aware batch merging and kernel scheduling improvements. Measured 10-18% throughput improvement on mixed-length workloads and 12% latency tail reduction in our canary region.
description: Motivation: Mixed-length workloads cause excessive padding in continuous batching which wastes GPU cycles and increases latency. This PR implements sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics, integrates KV-cache awareness into batch formation, and improves kernel selection scheduling to prefer low-padding batches when throughput would benefit. Summary: 1) New bucketing algorithm (heuristics.py) that maintains multiple active buckets by approximate seqlen percentiles and dynamically moves requests to the smallest bucket that keeps utilization targets, 2) Padding minimization policy that prefers forming a slightly smaller batch to avoid a large padding blowup, 3) KV-cache-aware merge that avoids combining batches whose KV cache locality would thrash memory and instead schedules them sequentially, 4) Kernel selector updates to bias optimized kernels for the typical bucket sizes, 5) Continuous batching loop changes to quickly close small bins under low load while still allowing aggressive merging under high QPS. Design notes: The bucketing is O(1) per request amortized, uses a tiny moving histogram for seqlen distribution, and exposes tunables via default_batching.yaml. KV-cache flags are consulted at batch-formation time; when KV incompatibility is detected the batcher prefers coalescing by KV namespace or deferring. Benchmarks: microbench harness shows 10-18% throughput improvement on mixed-length traces, 8-12% reduction in p95 latency. CI: added unit tests for bucket assignment and padding minimizer, integration test for KV-aware merge, and end-to-end benchmark job. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag 'seqlen_bucketing_v30', staged rollout to Dedicated pools then Hosted with canary, metrics monitored: effective tokens/sec, avg padding ratio, KV cache hit rate, p95 latency. Related: builds on previous v29 heuristics and addresses issues in ENG-3242 about padding regressions. Backwards compat: default behavior unchanged until flag enabled. Changes: See files_changed. Tests: added deterministic tests and new microbench scenario. Documentation: perf doc updated with guidance for tuning bucket thresholds and expected tradeoffs.

review_comments: Ethan Liu: Can you explain how the moving histogram avoids oscillation under sudden workload shifts?
Maya Chen: The histogram uses exponential decay with a short half-life and a smoothing window; we also backoff bucket reassignments if recent reassignment rate is high.
Ravi Desai: Kernel selection seems to prefer fp16 conv kernels by default for bucket size 128, what about older GPUs?
Maya Chen: Added fallback to generic kernel path based on runtime capability probe; documented behavior in kernel_selector.cpp comments.
Priya Nambiar: Please add a canary metric for effective padding ratio and a flag to disable KV-aware merging.
Maya Chen: Added metric 'batch.avg_padding_ratio' and config flag 'enabled_kv_merge' in default_batching.yaml.
Ethan Liu: Approving after tests are green.
merge_notes: Squashed and merged after approvals. Feature gated and rolled out to dedicated pools in canary fashion. Observability dashboards added for rollout monitoring.
notes_for_backport: No backport required; runtime flag controls behavior. If backporting to stable branch, ensure kernel selector probes exist for older GPU drivers.
short_summary: Implements sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics with KV-cache-aware batching and kernel scheduling tweaks, improving throughput and tail latency for mixed-length workloads.
